public_rationale: Crunchbase reports continuing AI seed investment globally and $61 billion in North American AI-focused funding rounds in Q3 2026 [e1, e2]. These reports do not establish the sector-wide funding withdrawal needed to test the forecast [e1, e2]. They also provide no fixed-cohort survival results after such a withdrawal, so they neither establish nor refute the predicted majority failure [e1, e2].
limitations: Aggregate investment does not show whether individual startups can obtain financing.
Both reports draw on Crunchbase data, which is subject to reporting lags.
The packet lacks a fixed publication-date startup cohort and comprehensive closure and survival records.
The forecast specifies neither a deadline nor how far or how long financing must fall to count as drying up.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most AI startups will die once venture capital subsidies dry up.
conditions: once venture capital subsidies dry up

statement.excerpt: I believe the vast majority of these data centers go unused and/or unfinished, and that most AI startups will die once the venture capital subsidies dry up.

from_speaker: once the venture capital subsidies dry up
our_interpretation: Treat this as conditional on a broad withdrawal of venture financing from AI startups, rather than one company's unsuccessful fundraising.
Interpret 'most' as more than half by company count.
Interpret 'die' as business closure or insolvency ending the operating business. An acquisition, IPO or valuation decline alone does not count.
Use the AI-startup population operating at publication, with survival after the funding withdrawal assessed consistently.
No deadline is supplied for either the funding withdrawal or subsequent failures.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented sector-wide withdrawal of venture financing, more than half of the defined startup cohort permanently cease operating.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After that withdrawal, a definitive follow-up establishes that at least half of the cohort survived the funding transition as continuing businesses. Continuing funding before the antecedent is not a contradiction of the conditional forecast.

evidence.explanation: The report records substantial global AI financing in the third quarter and continuing seed investment. This weighs against the required sector-wide funding withdrawal; it does not contradict the conditional failure prediction.
The North American report independently details continuing AI financing within the same underlying dataset. A quarterly decline is not equivalent to venture financing drying up across the sector.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Document a sector-wide withdrawal of venture financing and track a fixed cohort of AI startups operating on May 26, 2026. Permanent closure of more than half would support the forecast. A definitive follow-up establishing that at least half survived the funding transition would contradict it; survival over an arbitrary short interval would not suffice.
